name: Hal Jackman
current_role: Patriarch / largest family shareholder of E-L Financial Corporation (Toronto); former Lieutenant Governor of Ontario
profile: Henry N.R. 'Hal' Jackman (b. 1932) expanded the insurance and investment empire built by his father Harry Jackman, chairing National Trust and Empire Life; the family controls TSX-listed E-L Financial, now run by his son Duncan. He was Ontario's 25th Lieutenant Governor (1991-97) and U of T chancellor (1997-2003). In 2025 he gave $80M to U of T law, renamed the Henry N.R. Jackman Faculty of Law.
interesting_fact: His September 2025 $80 million gift was the largest ever to a Canadian law school, bringing his giving to U of T's law faculty to $100 million; the school was renamed the Henry N.R. Jackman Faculty of Law.
deep_cut_fact: While Lieutenant Governor in 1991, Jackman donated his historic collection of toy soldiers (over 650 figures) to the Royal Ontario Museum; he also served as honorary colonel of the Governor General's Horse Guards, a Toronto militia unit.
notes: Aged 94; no personal public channels. E-L Financial press releases name CFO Scott F. Ewert as the contact (published business line (416) 947-2578). Honorary-colonel detail from U of T/Victoria College sources: https://vic.utoronto.ca/henry-n-r-jackman-honoured-with-international-business-lnew-news-page

name: NR Narayana Murthy
current_role: Founder and Chairman Emeritus, Infosys; founder of family investment firm Catamaran Ventures
profile: N.R. Narayana Murthy (b. 1946) co-founded Infosys in 1981 with six colleagues, seeded by Rs 10,000 from his wife Sudha Murty, and built it into one of India's largest IT services companies, serving as CEO and chairman. Often called the father of the Indian IT sector, he is now Chairman Emeritus and invests via Catamaran Ventures.
interesting_fact: He has said being arrested and expelled near the Yugoslav-Bulgarian border in 1974, while hitchhiking back from Europe, turned him from a 'confused leftist' into a 'compassionate capitalist'.
deep_cut_fact: Before Infosys, as chief systems programmer at IIM Ahmedabad he worked on India's first time-sharing computer system and designed a BASIC interpreter for ECIL; his first startup, Softronics, folded after about a year and a half.
notes: Infosys press email reaches the company, not him directly; Catamaran Ventures (his family office, catamaranventures.com) may be a more direct route but no published email was verified. Gives frequent public lectures and interviews, often on work ethic and entrepreneurship.

name: Carlos March Delgado
current_role: Vice president, Fundación Juan March; former chairman of Corporación Financiera Alba (until Sept 2025) and Banca March (1974-2015)
profile: Grandson of financier Juan March, Carlos March Delgado (b. 1945, Palma) chaired family-owned Banca March for four decades until 2015 and Corporación Financiera Alba until September 2025, when his son Juan March de la Lastra succeeded him after Alba was taken private by the family. With brother Juan he controls most of Banca March and Alba.
interesting_fact: Banca March, founded by his grandfather in Palma de Mallorca in 1926, is Spain's only 100% family-owned bank; Carlos left its board in 2024 and handed the Alba chair to his son in 2025.
deep_cut_fact: He graduated in law from Madrid's Complutense University in 1965 as number one in his class, and later served as vice chairman of France's Carrefour and on JPMorgan's International Council.
notes: Low public profile, rarely gives interviews. Alba email is the company's general contact (Alba is family-owned since delisting). Fundación Juan March (march.es) is another institutional route.

name: Erman Ilicak
current_role: Founder and President Emeritus (Honorary President), Ronesans Holding; board chaired by his daughter Ipek Ilicak Kayaalp
profile: Turkish engineer Erman Ilicak founded Ronesans in 1993 in St. Petersburg and built it into a contractor and developer active in some 28 countries (about $50B of projects, ~70% abroad), later adding PPP hospitals, real estate and energy/petrochemicals. Now President Emeritus, he champions heavy-industry investment such as the Ceyhan petrochemical cluster with a $2B polypropylene plant.
interesting_fact: Ilicak started Ronesans in St. Petersburg, Russia, where he had worked as an engineer for billionaire Sinan Tara's Enka; Ronesans later bought Dutch contractor Ballast Nedam (2015).
deep_cut_fact: A basketball player at Ankara's TED high school, he later served as president of the TED Ankara Sports Club (TED Ankara Kolejliler) from 2014 to 2016.
notes: Energy/industrial angle: vocal on industrial policy and the Ceyhan (DAPEK) petrochemical zone, speaks at Turkish economic summits. Corporate Relations email listed for both Ankara and Istanbul offices.

name: Chan Tan Ching-fen
current_role: Matriarch and largest shareholder of Hang Lung Group (Hong Kong)
profile: Chan Tan Ching-fen is the widow of Hang Lung Group founder Chan Tseng-hsi (T.H. Chan, d. 1986) and controls the largest shareholding in the Hong Kong property developer. Her son Ronnie Chan ran Hang Lung until 2024, when grandson Adriel Chan became chair; son Gerald leads Morningside Group.
interesting_fact: Her father, Tan Hui-kuk, was a second cousin of Sun Yat-sen, founding father of the Republic of China, and provided Sun with financial support.
deep_cut_fact: Trained as a nurse, in the 1950s she gave cholera vaccinations to neighbourhood children in the family kitchen; her sons later named Harvard's T.H. Chan School of Public Health after her husband with a $350M gift in 2014.
notes: Alive status based on her live Forbes real-time listing (Nov 2026); age not published and she is very elderly and entirely private. Not a realistic podcast guest; family business-facing figures are Ronnie, Gerald and Adriel Chan. Web-search budget ran out during this lane, so status not separately verified.

name: Remo Ruffini
current_role: Executive Chairman, Moncler S.p.A. (since 1 April 2026, when Bartolomeo Rongone became CEO); controls holding company Double R
profile: Como-born Remo Ruffini (b. 1961) took over near-bankrupt Moncler in 2003 and turned it into a global luxury brand, listing it in Milan in 2013 and buying Stone Island for about EUR 1.15B in 2020. He owns roughly 15% via Double R and in 2026 moved from chairman-CEO to executive chairman.
interesting_fact: Moncler's December 2013 IPO was one of Italy's largest in years; shares jumped 47% on the first afternoon, putting Ruffini on the Forbes billionaires list in 2014.
deep_cut_fact: At 23, after working in the U.S. for his father's company Gianfranco Ruffini Ltd, he went home to Como and founded his own label, New England, which he sold to the Stefanel Group 16 years later.
notes: Moncler Group site (press and IR contact pages) blocked automated access; press/IR contacts are listed there under Media / Investor Relations and on Moncler press releases. No verified personal social accounts found.

name: Maria Dolores Mantegazza
current_role: Heir and shareholder of the Globus family of travel brands (Globus, Cosmos, Avalon Waterways, Monograms; U.S. arm Group Voyagers); trustee, Sergio Mantegazza Charitable Foundation
profile: Maria Dolores Mantegazza (b. 1956) is the daughter of Sergio Mantegazza (1927-2024), longtime owner-chairman of Lugano-based Globus, the escorted-tour group behind Globus, Cosmos, Avalon Waterways and Monograms. She appeared on Hurun's 2024 global list after inheriting a share of the family fortune on her father's death in February 2024.
interesting_fact: The Globus travel empire traces back to 1928, when her grandfather Antonio Mantegazza started out with a single gondola carrying tourists and goods on Lake Lugano.
deep_cut_fact: She is a trustee, with Fabio and Geo Mantegazza, of the Sergio Mantegazza Charitable Foundation in Canton Ticino, which supports arts, youth sports, education and medical charities.
notes: Extremely private; no interviews or public channels found. Alive status inferred from Hurun 2024 listing, not independently confirmed (web-search budget exhausted). Globus press pages blocked automated access; best route is the Globus/Group Voyagers corporate press office.

name: Sun Jimu
current_role: Founder/chairman of Handan Zongheng Steel Group (Sinogiant), Hebei, China (latest verified role)
profile: Sun Jimu (b. 1956, Shaoxing, Zhejiang) built Handan Zongheng Steel Group, the private Hebei steelmaker trading as Sinogiant, serving as chairman and general manager. He has been on Hurun's China list since 2007, with wealth shared with Sun Chunli. He also served as a Hebei deputy to the 11th and 12th National People's Congress.
interesting_fact: A Zhejiang native who studied agronomy, he built his steel business far from home in Handan, Hebei, China's steel heartland, and was twice elected a national legislator (NPC deputy) for Hebei in 2008 and 2013.
deep_cut_fact: Before steel, he trained in agronomy at Zhejiang's Shaoxing agricultural college.
notes: Very low international profile; Chinese-language sources only. Company websites blocked automated access and web-search budget was exhausted, so current role and status are not verified past the NPC terms; treat as unconfirmed. Sinogiant = Zongheng (纵横) Steel per Hurun naming; relationship to Sun Chunli not verified.

name: Hu Kaijun
current_role: Chairman and CEO, China Grand Enterprises (Beijing); chairman/CEO of Beijing Yuanda Huachuang Investment
profile: Hu Kaijun heads China Grand Enterprises, a Beijing-based investment group with interests in healthcare, real estate, agriculture and financial services and parent of Hong Kong-listed Grand Pharmaceutical, Shenzhen-listed Huadong Medicine and Grand Industrial Holding. His wealth stems mainly from the stakes in Huadong Medicine and Grand Pharmaceutical.
interesting_fact: In 2023 Grand Pharmaceutical agreed to buy 87.5% of U.S.-based vascular drug maker BlackSwan Vascular for $37.5 million, part of its push into innovative cardiovascular and interventional products.
notes: Very low media profile; no interviews or personal channels found. Grand Pharma IR (Hong Kong) is the most reachable published channel. No sourced deep-cut fact found (web-search budget exhausted).

name: Wang Ping
current_role: Co-founder/major shareholder of Shenzhen Megmeet Electrical (SZSE: 002851), per Hurun; exact current title not verified
profile: Hurun lists Wang Ping, alongside chairman Tong Yongsheng, as a principal owner of Shenzhen Megmeet Electrical, a power-electronics maker founded in 2003 and listed in Shenzhen in 2017. Megmeet makes power supplies, EV drivetrain parts, industrial automation and appliance controls, and since 2023 has pushed into AI data-center (AIDC) power, with orders topping RMB 10B in 2025.
interesting_fact: Megmeet now pitches itself as a 'cornerstone of global computing-power infrastructure': its catalogue includes CRPS server power supplies, power shelves, BBU shelves and an 800V/570kW side rack for AI data centers.
notes: Highly relevant to a data-center/energy podcast via Megmeet's AI-server power business, but Wang Ping's personal role is unverified (common name; company management page did not list her/him). Web-search budget was exhausted; check Megmeet's annual report on cninfo before outreach. Tong Yongsheng is the company's public face.

name: Ioannis Papalekas
current_role: Founder and ~66% shareholder of YODA PLC (Cyprus Stock Exchange-listed investment group); based in Nicosia
profile: Greek investor Ioannis Papalekas (about 50) made his name developing commercial real estate in Romania, then founded Globalworth, listing it in London in 2013 and selling his 13.5% stake for $315M in 2020. He founded YODA in 2019 and listed it in Cyprus in 2022; it invests in shipping and energy, hospitality, healthcare, technology and Greek/Cypriot real estate.
interesting_fact: Before founding Globalworth, his Romanian commercial real-estate developments reportedly earned a 175% rate of return for him and his investors.
deep_cut_fact: YODA listed on the Cyprus Stock Exchange's Emerging Companies Market in 2022 at EUR 0.50 a share, and in 2023 began buying Nasdaq-listed shipping/energy stock CCEC.
notes: Low media profile. YODA's general inbox is the only published channel found; IR announcements at yoda.com.cy/investor-relations/announcements/. Shipping/energy holdings give a possible energy angle.

name: Wee Ee Lim
current_role: President & CEO, Haw Par Corporation (Tiger Balm); Chairman, UOL Group and Singapore Land Group; Director, United Overseas Bank
profile: Wee Ee Lim (64), son of late UOB patriarch Wee Cho Yaw, joined Tiger Balm maker Haw Par in 1986 and has been its president and CEO since 2003. After his father's death he became chairman of property developer UOL Group (2024) and Singapore Land Group, and sits on UOB's board; his wealth includes his share of the family stakes inherited in 2025.
interesting_fact: He has run Haw Par, owner of the century-old Tiger Balm ointment brand, for over two decades, while also chairing two listed property groups and serving on the board of UOB, one of Singapore's three big banks.
deep_cut_fact: He studied economics in the U.S. at Clark University in Worcester, Massachusetts (BA Economics), and joined Haw Par's board in 1994, nine years before becoming CEO.
notes: Low-key; rarely interviewed. He is also a director of the family's Wee Foundation. UOL site blocked automated access; UOL's corporate communications contact is listed on uol.com.sg.

name: Ajay Jaisinghani
current_role: Promoter-group shareholder of Polycab India (wires, cables and electrical goods), Mumbai
profile: Ajay Jaisinghani owes his fortune to a minority stake in Polycab India, the wires-and-cables maker that his brother Inder Jaisinghani (chairman and MD) started as a trading firm in 1986. Polycab makes power, solar and optical-fibre cables for power, oil and gas and renewables, plus fans, lighting and switchgear, and has boomed since its 2019 IPO on electrification and grid spending.
interesting_fact: Polycab's growth since its 2019 listing has been driven by India's electrification push and power-sector spending; it supplies cables for power, oil and gas and renewable-energy projects.
notes: Not on Polycab's current board/key-people page (brother Inder is CMD; Bharat and Nikhil Jaisinghani are executive directors), so he is a low-profile shareholder; the company is the only published route. Strong energy/grid angle via Polycab. No sourced deep-cut fact found (web-search budget exhausted).

name: Lin Zhong
current_role: Founder and chairman, CIFI Holdings (Xuhui / 旭辉, HKEX: 0884), Shanghai (as last reported; not re-verified for 2026)
profile: Lin Zhong founded Shanghai-based property developer CIFI (Xuhui) in 2000 and took its holding company public in Hong Kong in 2012. CIFI grew into a top-30 Chinese developer, with total assets of RMB 256B and revenue of RMB 47.8B in 2024, spanning housing, commercial complexes, property services and senior care. He dropped off Hurun's lists after 2022 amid China's property downturn.
interesting_fact: CIFI ranked 13th among Shanghai's top 100 private enterprises in 2023 and 27th among Chinese real-estate developers by overall strength in 2024.
notes: CIFI has been through offshore debt restructuring since 2022-23; outreach should be sensitive to that. Last on Hurun lists in 2022. Current title and status not re-verified because the web-search budget ran out. CIFI site also has a media-contact page (媒体联络).

name: Lawrence Ho
current_role: Chairman and CEO, Melco International Development and Melco Resorts & Entertainment (Nasdaq: MLCO); founder of family office Black Spade Capital
profile: Lawrence Ho, eldest living son of the late Stanley Ho, left investment banking in 2001 to take a 26% stake in Melco International and built Melco Resorts into a major integrated-resort operator: City of Dreams and Studio City in Macau, City of Dreams Manila and Europe's largest integrated resort, City of Dreams Mediterranean in Cyprus (2023). His Black Spade Capital invests in SPACs, tech and green energy.
interesting_fact: His Black Spade SPAC merged with Vietnamese EV maker VinFast in a $23 billion Nasdaq listing in 2023; Black Spade's remit also covers green energy and, reportedly, space-sector deals.
deep_cut_fact: Before casinos he began in September 1999 in Jardine Fleming's Asia derivatives group (then Citibank), and in 2003 Melco's Mocha Clubs pioneered café-style slot parlours in Macau.
notes: Media-friendly CEO who speaks at conferences; Black Spade Capital (family office, Hong Kong) is a second route for non-gaming topics such as green energy and SPACs. Toronto-educated (Upper Canada College, U of T BCom 1999).
